content: Confirmed refresh token rotation is also enforced in the OAuth2 callback path, not just the /refresh endpoint. The server-side invalidation behavior is consistent across all auth flows.
Login rate limiting keys on device fingerprint in addition to email and IP. The email+IP-only understanding from the previous session was incomplete — all three factors combine.
Password reset tokens and login session tokens use separate revocation stores. Resetting a password does not invalidate active sessions, which is intentional per the auth spec.
Service accounts authenticate via signed JWTs and bypass the email/password login path entirely, so login rate limits do not apply to them.
Re-verified that the JWT middleware rejects requests missing either sub or org_id. Behavior unchanged from last session.
Wondering whether CORS preflight caching interacts with token expiry for cross-origin auth requests. Have not verified yet.
The auth_sessions table currently has 4 columns.
